boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Florida State traditions spanning game day, Homecoming, campus landmarks and ceremonial milestones.

cards.title: Watch Osceola and Renegade
cards.subtitle: FSU football pregame tradition
cards.notes: See the university-sanctioned portrayal in its designated game-day setting, and use FSU’s current event guidance for any viewing details.
cards.short_summary: A student portrayal of Osceola rides Renegade as a signature FSU game-day tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU states that the Osceola and Renegade tradition began in 1978 in consultation with the Seminole Tribe of Florida.
cards.source_title: Path to Partnership | Relationship with the Seminole Tribe of Florida
cards.access_notes: Appearances are controlled by parameters established with the Seminole Tribe of Florida; check current game information.

cards.title: Recognize the War Chant
cards.subtitle: Florida State Athletics tradition
cards.notes: Listen for the Marching Chiefs’ arrangement at an FSU game or official performance, and follow venue guidance on participation.
cards.short_summary: The chant grew from a revived Marching Chiefs melody into a stadium-wide FSU tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: Florida State Athletics documents that the current War Chant emerged from a 1984 Auburn game and became stadium-wide by 1986.
cards.source_title: The War Chant | Florida State University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Check the hosting event’s current attendance and venue rules.

cards.title: Learn the Sod Game ritual
cards.subtitle: FSU football’s practice-field memorial
cards.notes: Read the marked victories and the origin story before a game; the cemetery records qualifying road-win turf returned by team captains.
cards.short_summary: A practice-field cemetery preserves opponent turf from qualifying FSU football victories.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Athletics says victorious captains return qualifying opponents’ turf to be buried in the Sod Cemetery.
cards.source_title: The Sod Cemetery | Florida State University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Located inside the practice-field gates; view only when the area is open to the public.

cards.title: Dip a class ring at 6:51
cards.subtitle: Westcott Fountain ring ceremony
cards.notes: If you buy an official FSU class ring, attend the annual ceremony and join the fountain ring dip at the documented 6:51 p.m. finale.
cards.short_summary: Class-ring recipients conclude the ceremony by dipping their rings at Westcott Fountain.
cards.evidence_claim: The FSU Alumni Association identifies the Ring Ceremony and 6:51 p.m. Westcott Fountain ring dip as an FSU tradition for ring purchasers.
cards.source_title: FSU Class Rings | FSU Alumni Association
cards.access_notes: Available to students who purchase an official class ring; consult the Alumni Association for annual ceremony details.

cards.title: Follow the Chief and Princess coronation
cards.subtitle: FSU Homecoming court tradition
cards.notes: Watch for the Homecoming court presentation and learn how Seminole-made turbans are part of the ceremony’s continuing partnership history.
cards.short_summary: FSU Homecoming’s Chief and Princess are crowned with turbans made and presented by Tribal members.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU states that Seminole Tribal members make and present turbans to the Homecoming Chief and Princess each year.
cards.source_title: Path to Partnership | Relationship with the Seminole Tribe of Florida
cards.access_notes: The coronation is part of FSU Homecoming; consult current Homecoming programming for viewing details.

cards.title: See the Unconquered spear burn
cards.subtitle: Doak Campbell Stadium game-weekend ritual
cards.notes: Visit the statue from public areas on a home-game weekend to see the spear-lighting tradition, while respecting posted stadium access rules.
cards.short_summary: The Unconquered statue’s spear is lit overnight around each FSU home football game.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU says Unconquered’s spear is ignited at sunset before each home game and burns until sunrise the following morning.
cards.source_title: Seminole Presence on Campus | Relationship with the Seminole Tribe of Florida
cards.access_notes: The lighting occurs on home-game weekends; observe from permitted public areas and follow posted access rules.

cards.title: Know Torch Night
cards.subtitle: Garnet and Gold Key recognition tradition
cards.notes: Look for this annual recognition of incoming students and learn its connection to Garnet and Gold Key, FSU’s oldest leadership honorary.
cards.short_summary: Torch Night recognizes one hundred incoming freshmen through an FSU leadership-honorary tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU’s Registrar states that Garnet and Gold Key’s annual activities include Torch Night, which recognizes the top 100 incoming freshmen.
cards.source_title: Honors Office and Honor Societies | FSU University Registrar
cards.access_notes: Recognition is administered through Garnet and Gold Key; check current university announcements for event details.

cards.title: Catch a Skull Session
cards.subtitle: Marching Chiefs pregame performance
cards.notes: Attend an officially scheduled Skull Session to hear the Marching Chiefs before the game, using the event’s current entrance and timing information.
cards.short_summary: The Marching Chiefs’ Skull Session is a named pregame performance associated with FSU football weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Family Weekend directs visitors to the Marching Chiefs’ Skull Session performance at Dick Howser Stadium following Legacy Walk.
cards.source_title: Football Game & Tickets | FSU Family Weekend
cards.access_notes: The cited page schedules Skull Session after Legacy Walk; verify its current date, location and entrance instructions.

cards.title: Join Odds and Evens
cards.subtitle: FSU Homecoming field-game tradition
cards.notes: Form a team or watch the Homecoming field games, then consult the annual schedule for the specific sports, team rules and registration details.
cards.short_summary: Odds and Evens brings student groups together for recreational competition during Homecoming Week.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Homecoming calls Odds and Evens a university tradition combining Homecoming games including dodgeball, kickball, soccer and flag football.
cards.source_title: Light Your Legacy as FSU Celebrates the 75th Anniversary of Homecoming
cards.access_notes: Held during Homecoming Week; use the current FSU Homecoming schedule for participation details.

cards.title: Learn the FSU Fight Song
cards.subtitle: Official Florida State song tradition
cards.notes: Use the university’s official lyrics page to learn the song before an FSU event, and follow the lead of official performers in the venue.
cards.short_summary: Florida State publishes its Fight Song alongside its hymn and alma mater.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU’s Welcome site publishes the lyrics of the official FSU Fight Song.
cards.access_notes: Lyrics are publicly available online; event participation depends on the hosting venue’s rules.
